opening_message:
Ticket 1: Miguel Benson (employee ID E006) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E006.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Miguel Benson (E006) is a full-time Engineer. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is within policy for this employee. Requested admin, granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E006 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.
reason: HR records (authoritative for employment type and role) show Miguel Benson (E006) is a full-time Engineer. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is within policy for full-time employees whose role owns the system. The requested level (admin) equals the maximum allowed, so admin is granted. (Note: the Security agent's note lists E006 as a contractor, which conflicts with HR; I rely on HR for employment type, so the contractor restriction does not apply.)
